rationale: design-import-refactor: generic change landed in Pulp per owner decision 2026-10-04; Vellum inherits (see inheritance ledger); every Skia surface Pulp creates for drawing now takes an explicit canvas::TextRasterPolicy {legacy, chromium}, mapped to SkSurfaceProps by one helper (chromium = contrast 0, gamma 1). SkiaSurface (Graphite and WebGL2) and HeadlessSurface take it in Config and through set_text_raster_policy(), which drops retained layers and recreates the offscreen and scene targets; retained layers inherit the props of the canvas they are recorded from; the raster and GPU screenshot paths and the plugin raster renderer take a trailing policy argument. select_text_raster_policy() returns chromium when any text node is antialiased. legacy is the default everywhere and equals a props-less surface, so no existing UI changes pixels; no design-import, Chromium, packaging or authority boundary moves, and the Pulp render target has not adopted a Vellum package.
tests: ctest --test-dir build -R 'a GPU surface carries its text raster policy into retained layers'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'a chromium surface changes how text rasterizes'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'an auto span on a chromium surface stays within the ink band'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'legacy surface props are the props a surface gets without any'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'text raster policy turns chromium when any text node is antialiased'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'text raster tuples are the measured contrast and gamma'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'text through a retained layer matches direct paint under each policy'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'the persistent scene target carries the surface'
ctest --test-dir build -R 'the widget gallery renders unchanged under the default policy'
